paquet:commande:C1.summary:
I built work package C1 (the contract, the order words, the cards, the repères and the adjoint's titles). The new tests and every existing test I re-ran pass, and `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` is clean. Nothing is wired into the screen yet: C3 and C6 do that.

What now exists (all under /tmp/claude-0/hunt/commande/crs-simulation):

- **The contract**, `src/ui/command/cardTypes.ts`: every type of §8.0 with no logic. That covers repères, intentions, line actions, card lines, cards and the narrow card environment (`CardEnv`). It also holds the types the other packages need for who to send, the preview, sending a line and the legal chain.
- **Order words**, `src/ui/command/orders.ts`: every verb now has `plain`, `tag`, `explain` and `doing`, with the texts of §3.1. Other changes:
  - The order families are renamed « Se placer », « Se déplacer », « Face à la foule », « Intervenir », « Fin d'action ».
  - `EXTRA_PLAIN` holds the texts for `retour_poste` (« Rentrer au commissariat », tag RENTRE), so they work as soon as P5 adds the verb.
  - Force levels are words: `FORCE_WORDS`, `forceWord(level)` and `authorizeWord(level)` (« autoriser le gaz »). No digit is ever shown.
  - New helpers: `tagOf(type, targetId)` (gives « BARRE (PASSANTS) », and '' for an unknown type), `plainOf`, `doingAt` (« Barre la rue de Rivoli ») and `withArticle`.
  - `orderLabel()` now returns the plain tag (« En ligne », « Sans ordre »).
  - `verbOf` re-indexes when P5 adds a verb.
- **Cards and intentions**, `src/ui/command/intents.ts`:
  - The six intentions on keys E B N D I S; B, I and S are sticky. Also the « Plus… » button data and the legal-chip tooltip.
  - `buildCard` builds every card of §2.3: street, crowd, kettle, incident, my unit, unit not mine, VOUS, point, blocking vehicle, metro, road closure, adjoint's proposal and police station. It follows the plan's rules:
    - at most 6 lines, plus « Autres ordres ici… »;
    - « Y aller » walks in file, or in formation within 60 m of a crowd;
    - street line 1 is targetId 0, line 2 is targetId −2;
    - « Fermer aux voitures » appears only with traffic rights;
    - the intention's default line is always among the six visible lines (it takes line 6's place if needed);
    - the legal marks: 🔒 shows what is missing (« sommations 0/3 + autoriser le gaz »), ⚖ marks force before the last sommation, and nothing is marked when riposte is allowed;
    - read-only players get no lines; a chef de groupe gets no metro or station lines;
    - station lines are numbered without gaps.
  - `intentCandidates` ranks places for each intention. For B: unheld exit streets first, the main crowd first, streets ahead of the march first, then streets already held.
  - `allOrdersGrouped()` lists every order by family.
  - There are registries for P5 (`registerCardBuilder`, `registerCardLines`, plus `registerRepereProvider` re-exported from `reperes.ts`). How to use them is documented in the file's header comment.
- **Repères**, `src/ui/command/reperes.ts`:
  - `collectReperes`, `pickAt` (priority: my unit > incident > station > metro/closure > crowd > VOUS > street; a crowd can also be picked by its body), and `nextInDirection` (100° cone, score = distance × (1 + 2·angle)).
  - `cardEnvFromCore(core, selection)` fills the card environment from the running game: scene, scope, law, law advisor, proposals, `police.obstacle`, real streets and place names.
  - `registerCardEnvHook` lets P5 fill in stations and home stations.
- **Adjoint titles**, `src/ui/command/adjointPlays.ts`: `proposalTitle` with the §6.3 titles. Unit and place names come from the radio text, and spelled digits become numbers (« QUATRE-ZÉRO » → 40). An unknown key falls back to the cleaned radio text (no PARLEZ, TERMINÉ or call signs).

Titles were added for keys §6.3 does not list but the code proposes: `fin`, `renfort:`, `incident:`, `fermeture:`, `poste:`, `metro:<id>` and `obstacle_voie` (both variants: Centaure, or « faire circuler par X »). The verb `plain` texts are generic (e.g. interpeller « Interpeller ici », proteger « Protéger une autre unité… », degager_barricade « Dégager une barricade »); the cards use the contextual labels of §3.1. `doing` texts are mine (the plan gives none).

C1B: a unit card's Qui is `card.whoFixed`. A `means` line's default Qui is `action.squadId`. A `rescue` line on an incident carries `incidentId` (request plus assign, like `PanelIncidents.delegate`). Metro `filter` and `closeRoad` use Qui as the holder.

P5 (commissariats): add `retour_poste` to `ORDER_VERBS` with group 'fin' (its texts are already in `EXTRA_PLAIN`). Then fill `env.stations` and each unit's `CardUnit.homeStation` through `registerCardEnvHook`, or register its own builder with `registerCardBuilder('commissariat', …)`. Until the verb exists, the « Rentrer au commissariat » line stays hidden.

C5 / C7: `orderLabel` now returns « En ligne » / « Sans ordre » / « Barre »; the HUD unit chip should use `tagOf(type, targetId)` for « MISTRAL 1 ALFA · EN LIGNE ». The overlay's `ORDER_TAGS` (C2) should equal `tagOf` for every verb.

`cardEnvFromCore` reads `core.maps.scene` (it calls `ensureFresh`) and loops over the squads to find which units have vehicles. Calling it at C3's 10 Hz card refresh is fine; it should not run every frame.

paquet:commande:C1B.summary:
I built work package C1B. It covers who to send, the automatic line, the preview, sending a card line and the legal chain. The four new test files pass (22/22) and `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` is clean. Nothing is shown on screen yet: C6 has to plug these functions into the screen (see openIssues).

What now exists, under /tmp/claude-0/hunt/commande/crs-simulation/src/ui/command:

- **Who (`bestUnit.ts`)**: `proposeWho(line, where, env)` returns the candidate units, best first.
  - Units the player already chose come first, exactly as chosen.
  - Then my units, excluding any the stations module marks "au poste" (`env.exclude`). Free units come first, then busy ones, then units holding a barrage, then units below 60 % strength. Busy and holding units are marked « (la quittera) ».
  - Fitness by order: barring and moving want a section, never the company; a group only if no section is free. A street wider than a section's front gets two sections (« Sections X et Y », « rue de 30 m : 2 sections »). Interpeller wants the BRAV-M, then the nearest group. Pushing a vehicle wants a Centaure. Clearing a barricade wants the Centaure, then a group. Gas wants a section that still has grenades. An incident line puts its named unit first. « Fermer aux voitures » starts with « Personne : barrières seules ».
  - Station reinforcements come last and are never picked by default (`defaultWho` skips them; `noUnitText` gives « Aucune unité libre — renfort possible : … : U »).
  - Also: `wholeCandidate` (what T selects: « Toute la compagnie / la section / Tout le groupe »), `travel` and `travelText` (« à pied · 180 m · ~2 min »), and `whoEnvFromCore(core, card, selection, {exclude, stationCandidates})`.
- **Automatic line (`autoLine.ts`)**:
  - On a street: across the road, façade to façade (road width), facing the crowd.
  - On a point: perpendicular to the crowd's direction, width = min(agents × 0.7 × 1.1, 40 m).
  - « Contenir »: the line sits at the crowd's edge on the units' side.
  - The two ends come out left flank first, so `issueLine` reads them exactly like a hand-drawn line.
- **Preview (`preview.ts`)**: `previewOf` gives the geometry C2 will draw. That covers the barred street (with passers-by and filter flags), one arrow per unit (« à pied · 2 min » / « en véhicules · 6 min »), the auto line, the nasse (each unit to its street), the tight circle, the gas cloud with the wind, the rescue point, a station route and the legal steps ①②③. `sentenceOf` builds « Ce qui va se passer : … » plus the order's rule. All texts are in French.
- **Sending (`sendLine.ts`)**: `sendCardLine` makes the same calls today's buttons make, after setting the selection to Qui. It covers:
  - orders: `issuePoint` / `issueLine` / `issueArea` / `issueImmediate`, and `core.issue` for a target;
  - nasse (proposeNasse then acceptNasse), filtered exit, road and area closures, rescue (assign then request, as the incidents panel does), handing an incident to a unit, unassign, cancelling a call;
  - metro, reopening streets, « Suivez-moi », the adjoint's proposal, sommations.
  - A station reinforcement is engaged with `core.engageFromCommissariat` and receives its order in the same tick.
  - A 🔒 line is never sent from here.
  - It returns the S4 text (« Section MISTRAL 2 → Barrer la rue de Rivoli, passants admis ») and the units that got the order.
  - Also: `lineSends`, `undoOrder` (« Annuler l'ordre » sends `cesser` to the same units), `legalCheck` (S3 steps and plan), `coreLegalDeps`, and `DirectIssuer`, which issues orders without the map so the chain works with the map closed.
- **Legal chain (`legalChain.ts`)**:
  - `legalSteps` lists S3's steps with the pre-checks: the sommations by the player or by the company officer, or a plain reason why nobody can (« Vous devez porter l'écharpe tricolore… »); authorise, or ask by radio; and for a chef de groupe, « Demander plus de force » with no chain.
  - `LegalChain` (`start` / `tick` / `cancel` / `status` / `active`) does each sommation once `sommationWait()` is 0. It asks the officer one step at a time when he is the one doing them, then authorises, waits `forceWait()`, and issues the order once.
  - It stops on a refusal with the reason, or after a radio force request with « … — en attente de l'autorisation du gaz ».
  - Status texts read like « Dispersion au gaz — sommation 2 sur 3 dans 25 s ».
- **`core.ts`**: new `readonly legalChain`, and an optional `engageFromCommissariat?` declared with no body (P5 provides it). `issue`, `check`, `authorize` and `callFollow` are unchanged.
- **`index.ts`**: `CommandSystem.update()` calls `core.legalChain.tick(ctx.clock.now)` every simulation step, so the chain runs with the map closed. The chain is reset on `session:started`.

- If the sommation series restarts (the law resets it after the authority moves), the chain goes back and redoes the sommations.
- If the officer has not pronounced a requested sommation after 150 s, the chain stops with a reason.
- Final statuses stay visible for a few seconds (« ordre donné » 6 s, « annulé » 4 s, refusal 20 s, waiting for authorisation 120 s), then `status()` returns null.

Instead it waits until some crowd has exits held by my units (at least one; up to two if it happens within 120 s of play), then checks that line 1 of the kettle card gives `filtrer` to the unit holding the widest held exit. paquet:commande:C3.summary:
I built work package C3, the screen of the command map. It runs in the real game with no page errors. It has the layout, the state machine (rest S0 → card S1 → Qui S2 → legal confirmation S3 → order given S4), the keys, the bottom bar of six intentions plus « Plus… », the phone sheets and the read-only map. Before C6 wires the other packages the right column stays empty and the screen sends no order; a plain arrow also still moves the free cursor until C2's `keyCursor` lands. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` is clean, and all tests I ran pass.

**What exists now**
- **`tacticalScreen.ts`** (rewritten):
  - **Top bar:** « CARTE DE COMMANDEMENT », and « vue partielle : vous êtes à pied » when the commandant is on foot. Phase, a tension gauge, crowd size and clock. The legal chip `tac-legal` (L, tooltip), « Vue drone » `tac-drone`, « Ralentir » / « Temps normal » `tac-slow` (V), « Fermer » `tac-close` (Tab). On the phone: « Suivi » `tac-suivi` with a badge.
  - **Map:** « Rechercher un lieu » `tac-search` (R, with results; Entrée puts the visée there and opens the card), « + », « − », « ◎ Moi » (G), wind rose and scale. An H help overlay with the exact §5.1 text, and the two-sentence model shown once at the first opening.
  - **Bottom bar:** `intent-<id>` buttons and « Plus… » `tac-more`, under the map only. Second lines are hidden below 1200 px, the bar is hidden while a card is open, and on the phone it is 52 px with buttons of at least 96 × 52 px inside the safe area.
  - **Right column:** 340 px, with three mount points (follow / card / sheet). On the phone it becomes one 380 px sheet at a time, the bar hides and the map re-centres the visée.
  - **Keyboard focus model (§2.0):**

- `intents.ts`: the incident card read « confié à les pompiers ». It now reads « aux pompiers » / « au SAMU », with a new unit assertion in `ui-command.fiches.test.ts`.

  - on the 2- to 4-sector wheels, the key numbers moved so they no longer sit on the second line of a side sector (« 2 » was over « toute mon unité »);
  - the notice now says « La carte reste consultable » instead of « la carte tactique ».
